name: Fried chicken meatballs, frozen (קציצות עוף מטוגנות קפואות)

source.author: Israeli frozen store product (label photo)
source.notes: Values transcribed directly from the Hebrew label — LABEL-VERIFIED, per 100 g (the label's own basis). Chicken meat 75%. Fried (refined soybean oil). Iron not on the label; estimated ~1 mg/100 g in the analysis only. Bone-fragment warning on pack (deboned but minimal presence possible).

ingredients.item: breadcrumbs (wheat flour, gluten, pea starch, yeast)
spices (contains celery), dietary fiber, salt, sugars, natural flavors

steps: Frozen pre-fried meatball — heat through before eating.

him.verdict: A convenience protein, not a standout. 16 g protein / 204 kcal (~7.8 g protein per 100 kcal) is only okay — dragged down by frying (12 g fat) and ~8 g of filler carb (soy protein + breadcrumbs). On the plus side for your sperm goal, it's poultry (not processed red meat) and trans fat is ≤0.5 g. Sodium 440 mg/100 g is moderate. Beats the Swedish beef version on the fertility lens, loses on raw protein density.
flags: poultry base (better fertility profile than processed red meat)
suggested_mods: Occasional convenience only — your homemade veg chicken meatballs (176 kcal, 15.5 g protein, no frying, no trans fat) beat it outright
Air-fry from frozen rather than pan-frying to avoid adding more oil
Serve over a big salad to offset the sodium/filler with fiber + micros

her_preconception.verdict: An okay protein top-up but not nutrient-dense: fried, ~440 mg sodium, only trace fiber, and less iron than the beef version (~1 mg/100 g est.). Fully cooked/frozen, so safe when reheated through. Contains gluten, soy, celery; may contain sesame, mustard, egg. The beef version gives her more iron + protein — better for the preconception iron priority.
prenatal_highlights: poultry, leaner saturated fat than the beef version

safety_advisories.note: Fully cooked then frozen — reheat until steaming hot before eating (standard for cooked frozen meat).

suggested_mods: Occasional; pair with iron/folate sides (greens, legumes)
Allergens: gluten, soy, celery; may contain sesame, mustard, egg

cooking_guide: Cook straight from frozen — don't thaw (thawing makes them soggy).
Best texture: oven or air-fryer at 200 C (400 F) ~12-15 min, turning once, until hot through and crisp — this re-crisps the coating without adding oil.
Or pan-heat over medium with little/no oil, turning, until browned and steaming hot inside.
Serve with a fresh salad or veg to balance the sodium. Tip: skip deep-frying — they're already fried, so oven/air-fry keeps them lighter.
